//: Ceilings for the single-file shells. Raise one IN THE COMMIT that needs the bytes, and say what bought them. Checked by scripts/test-spaces-size.mjs.

spaces.//: 224 KiB. Raised from 216 KiB by the starter space rewrite: 213,434 B before, 220,434 B after — +7,000 B, of which 5,336 B is prose and 1,664 B is the two files it ships (a hand-written SVG drawing and a 1.2s test tone, both chosen to deflate to almost nothing; see spaces/src/starterdata.ts). What bought it is the doctrine that a feature the starter does not demonstrate is a feature the starter denies: tables, clips, link cards, comments, calculating lines, daily notes, page width, export-a-page, subtree import, the mark palette, live collaboration and the properties panel had all shipped without ever appearing in the document every new user reads first. Headroom is deliberate: the shell is mostly one compressed block and the packer's output differs across node versions (one commit measured 130,095 B on node 26 locally and 131,246 B on CI node 24), so a tight ceiling fails in CI for no reason. CI is the number that counts.
